title: Debugging Mindset and Problem Decomposition
learningObjectives: Explain the concept in your own words
Identify the concept in a small example

understand.concept: Problem decomposition divides a large task into smaller parts with clear responsibilities. Debugging uses evidence to find the cause of unexpected behaviour: reproduce, inspect, form a hypothesis, change one thing and retest.
understand.whyItMatters: These ideas form the foundation for learning every programming language.
understand.history: This lesson focuses on transferable programming concepts; detailed language history is taught in the relevant language module.
understand.analogy: It is like writing clear instructions for a task and following them step by step.
understand.analogyLimit: Programming language rules are precise; a computer does not automatically infer ambiguity in casual human instructions.

explain.narrative: Problem decomposition divides a large task into smaller parts with clear responsibilities. Debugging uses evidence to find the cause of unexpected behaviour: reproduce, inspect, form a hypothesis, change one thing and retest.

practise.guidedTask: Choose a small everyday task and explain it using the idea of Debugging Mindset and Problem Decomposition.
